pride_data.title: Proximity labeling – LC/MS-MS with TurboID-ATG8e/atg2-1 Arabidopsis seedlings
pride_data.projectDescription: By employing a proximity labeling approach using Arabidopsis ATG8e tagged with TurboID as bait in atg2-1 background, we discovered a protein family of unknown function, consisting of two homologs (AT4G02880 and AT1G03290). Both proteins contain coil-coiled domains that are predicted to be closely related to the mammalian ELKS/Rab6-interacting/CAST (ERC) protein family, which acts as a central scaffold for forming a multidomain protein complex involved in synaptic vesicle secretion. As there is no available information about this protein family in plants, we have named these two proteins as ERC1 and ERC2, respectively.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Arabidopsis seedlings expressing TurboID-ATG8e under the UBQ10 promoter in atg2-1 or TurboID under the UBQ10 promoter were grown on ½ MS plates containing 1% sucrose for 5 days. Seedlings were harvested and submerged in ½ MS + 1% sucrose supplemented with 50 µM biotin for 1 h followed by washing and flash freezing. Proteins were extracted by resuspending the ground plant material in extraction buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT, 1× complete Protease inhibition cocktail, 1 mM PMSF), incubating for 15 minutes at 4°C on a rotor wheel, sonicating four times for 30 seconds and centrifuging at 15,000 g at 4°C for 15 minutes. The supernatants were buffer exchanged with PD-10 desalting columns to remove excess biotin from the extract using extraction buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT, 1× complete Protease inhibition cocktail, 1 mM PMSF). Eluted proteins were incubated with Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin T1 (Invitrogen, 150 μl) overnight at 4°C for affinity purification of biotinylated proteins. The beads were then washed with the following buffers: 2x with cold extraction buffer, 2x with equilibration buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT), 1x with cold 1M KCl, 1x with cold 100 mM Na2CO3, 1x with Urea wash buffer 1 (2 M Urea, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, room temperature) and 2x with 50 mM Tris pH 7.5. For on-beads tryptic digest, the streptavidin beads were further washed 2x with Urea wash buffer 2 (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 1 M Urea), followed by three hours incubation in Trypsin buffer (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 1 M Urea, 1m M DTT, 0.4 µg Trypsin) at 25°C. The supernatant from tryptic digest and two washes with 60 µl 1 M Urea in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5 were reduced and alkylated and digested overnight with 0.5 µg Trypsin. The digest was acidified by adding formic acid to a final concentration of ~ 1 % and desalted using OMIX C18 pipette tips.  LC-MS/MS analyses were performed on a Q-Exactive HF hybrid quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Easy-nLC 1200 UPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were initially concentrated on a trapping column (Acclaim PepMap 100 C18, 75 μm particle size, 2 cm bed length) and subsequently separated on an analytical column (AUR3-25075 C18, 25 cm × 75 μm, 1.7 μm, Aurora Series Emitter Column, IonOpticks) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. Peptide elution was achieved with a gradient from 3% to 28% solvent B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) over 101 min, followed by 28% to 44% solvent B over 20 min, and a final wash at 90% solvent B for 9 min. MS1 scans were acquired over an m/z range of 375–1,600, and the top 20 most intense multiply charged precursor ions were selected for fragmentation. Peptides were fragmented using higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 27, and the isolation window was set to 1.0 m/z.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Peptide identification and quantification of the mass spectrometry data was carried out using MaxQuant Version 2.4.12.0.  The data was searched against the Arabidopsis TAIR 10 protein database obtained from TAIR (TAIR10_pep_20101214.fasta) containing a total of 35386 entries and against the contaminants list of MaxQuant. All three control and experimental samples were analyzed simultaneously using the default settings with matching between runs turned on. Label free quantification (LFQ) was enabled with the minimum ratio count set to two. To analyze the resulting proteomic data, the identified protein groups and their LFQ intensities from the MaxQuant search were loaded into Perseus Version 2.1.3.0. Data were filtered to remove decoys, potential contaminants, and protein groups that were only identified by site (i.e., posttranslational modification). LFQ intensities were log2 transformed, and only protein groups that had valid values for either all three experimental samples or all three control samples were kept, an operation that eliminated non-reproducible identifications. Remaining invalid values were replaced with imputed values from a normal distribution downshifted by 1.8 with a width of 0.3 made from all matrix values. A two-sided T-test with S0 = 2 and FDR = 0.01 was used to determine the significance and enrichment of each protein group.
